pins.name: RUN
pins.description: RP2040 enable, pulled up inside (~50 kΩ): short to ground to reset

pins.name: AGND
pins.description: analog ground for GP26-28 (join to GND when the ADC is not critical)

pins.name: ADC_VREF
pins.description: the ADC's reference, filtered 3.3 V on the board

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: 3V3(OUT): the board's 3.3 V regulator output, keep loads under 300 mA

pins.name: 3V3_EN
pins.description: the regulator's enable, pulled up to VSYS (100 kΩ): short to ground to switch 3.3 V off

pins.name: VSYS
pins.description: the system supply, 1.8-5.5 V: from VBUS through a Schottky diode, or feed it here (through a diode when USB is used too)

pins.name: VBUS
pins.description: USB 5 V when the USB cable is plugged in (0 V otherwise)

notes: GPIOs are 3.3 V and not 5 V tolerant. In PCBKit 3V3 is `P3V3`, 3V3_EN `P3V3_EN`.
Power: USB (VBUS → diode → VSYS), or 1.8-5.5 V into VSYS; a second supply into VSYS goes through its own Schottky diode. 3V3 can feed sensors (under 300 mA).
The three SWD debug pins at the bottom edge are not in the socket. Pico W, Pico 2 and Pico 2 W have the same header pinout.
The USB connector overhangs the top edge (+Y): put that end at the board edge.

pins.source: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet, Figure 2 (pinout), Figure 4 (pin numbering), §2.1 (VBUS, VSYS, 3V3_EN, 3V3, ADC_VREF, AGND, RUN), Figure 3 (dimensions)
